title: Hypercortisolism: definitions, causes and metabolic effects
guide: Cushing's = hypercortisolism from zona fasciculata (75% of cortex). Causes: exogenous steroid (m/c), inherited AME, acquired ↑cortisol; pseudocushing = chronic stress of obesity/alcohol/depression. Cortisol (GC+MC)→cortisone (GC) via 11β-HSD2. Effects: protein catabolism → proximal myopathy; carbohydrate (adrenal diabetes) with gluconeogenesis alanine >> FFA; fat redistribution (centripetal, buffalo hump); MC triad HTN+mA+hypokalaemia; sex-steroid acne/hirsutism/amenorrhoea; CNS steroid psychosis.

title: Systemic effects, the eosinophil clue and the cause tree
guide: Eye ↑IOP/cataract/glaucoma; GI ulceration; ↓ linear growth; IL-6 inhibition (anti-inflammatory); ↑WBC yet infection-prone with eosinopenia and hypercoagulable thrombosis. Eosinopenia +infection → typhoid, −infection → Cushing's; eosinophilia → Addison's. Causes: ACTH-dependent 90% (pituitary adenoma 75% = Cushing's disease = m/c endogenous; paraneoplastic 15% m/c squamous cell carcinoma); ACTH-independent 10% (adenoma; carcinoma m/c in toddlers); others: McCune-Albright (GSα defect; triad precocious puberty/fibrous dysplasia/café-au-lait; m/c infancy) and PPNAD (micronodular, Carney's). Adult F>M.

title: Important symptoms, childhood Cushing's and first cut-offs
guide: Protein catabolism: B/L proximal symmetric myopathy (LL>UL), facial plethora (thin skin, lost SC fat), bruising, young-onset osteoporosis/fractures with short stature and delayed bone age, violaceous striae (loss of collagen). Plus DM/HTN metabolic syndrome and incidental adrenal mass + central obesity → screen. Childhood: m>>F, adrenal > pituitary, less catabolism, obesity, androgen → precocious puberty; Rx radiotherapy. Rule-out: midnight serum cortisol ≤1.8 µg/dL and salivary ≤5.5 mmol/L.

title: The diagnostic algorithm: diurnal rhythm, DSTs and ACTH
guide: 8 AM cortisol >1.8 µg/dl (loss of diurnal variation = earliest) → endogenous; too low → exogenous. ONDST 1 mg 11 pm → <1.8 rules out. LDDST 0.5 mg Q6H ×2d for pseudocushing/obesity/PCOS/OCP. ACTH <10 = adrenal (CT adrenal; U/L adenoma → unilateral adrenalectomy; B/L hyperplasia → B/L adrenalectomy with Nelson risk). ACTH >10: 10–50 pituitary, 50–100 both, >100 PNS (PET). MRI: ≥6 mm → hypophysectomy; <6 mm → IPSS; none → PET.

title: IPSS, high-dose DST, PNS and medical therapy
guide: IPSS petrosal/peripheral ACTH ratio >2:1 → pituitary adenoma → trans-sphenoidal hypophysectomy; <2 → PET → PNS. High-dose DST 2 mg Q6H ×2d, >50% suppression = pituitary. PNS: hyperpigmentation, less catabolism, MC action. TOC trans-sphenoidal surgery (75% remission); radiotherapy 3rd line; relapse-prevention drugs ketoconazole, pasireotide, cabergoline, metyrapone, mifepristone (GR inhibitor), mitotane (adrenolytic).
